flaws.title: Search joins the query text into SQL
flaws.why: search builds sql by concatenating query into the LIKE clause, so a crafted search reads or changes any table in the catalog database.

flaws.title: Price changes never reach the cache
flaws.why: set_price updates the database but never deletes or updates price_cache, and cached prices have no expiry, so old prices are served (and charged) forever.

flaws.title: Unknown product id crashes price lookup
flaws.why: fetchone() returns None for a missing id and row.price then raises, so a bad or deleted product id gives a server error instead of a not-found.

flaws.title: Product list and search return every row
flaws.why: list_products (and search, with a leading-wildcard LIKE) fetchall() with no LIMIT or paging, so load and response size grow with the whole catalog.

flaws.title: Price lookup fails when the cache is down
flaws.why: price_cache.get and price_cache.set are not guarded, so a Redis outage turns every price lookup into an error instead of falling back to the database.

flaws.title: Cached and database prices have different types
flaws.why: price_of returns raw bytes from Redis on a hit but the database value on a miss, so callers get b"9.99" one time and a number the next.
